scope: Read-only provider research and isolated browser QA. No product adapter, dist edit, build, release, native bridge, extension, credentials, account or runtime proxy added.
finding: Funkwhale public libraries provide a real additional music catalog with new exact canonical-reference matches across three artists. This is a coverage gain beyond generic transport controls, but not a solution for every unavailable commercial recording.

funkwhale.operator: The Funkwhale Collective, according to its public NodeInfo description.
funkwhale.stableMediaLocator: The selected public local upload's /api/v2/listen/{track-UUID}/?upload={upload-UUID}; metadata and permission checks precede media access.
funkwhale.v1Observation: The tested pod's v1 tracks route returned non-JSON; v2 tracks worked. Official API overview still describes v2 as work in progress, so a future adapter needs explicit version detection/validation rather than assuming a fixed stable schema.
discoveryChecks: Canonical catalog selected by title, artist, album and requested title_version, then hydrated from the same track ID.
Hydrated artist ID, album ID, normalized title/artist/album, exact numeric duration and title_version equal the selected row; canonical ISRC format validated.
Funkwhale candidate title, credited artist and album must match; require is_playable, content_category music, local public upload and duration within 3 seconds.
Do not treat metadata-only/private records with no accessible uploads, podcast matches or same-title other albums as playable replacements.
Construct/validate the pod-owned listen route from provider data; no arbitrary media URL or third-party extraction service.
Complete file fetched CORS with omitted credentials and checked against metadata byte length, bounded to 8 MiB per candidate.
SHA-256 of candidate, canonical preview and distinct negative preview computed before decoding; three-window acoustic comparison uses unchanged shared thresholds and consistent alignment.
Native Audio receives the exact fetched candidate bytes in a RAM-only Blob; one trusted click, seek and hidden-tab progression are recorded.
funkwhale.strictNegativeRetained: Kai Engel Collateral has a high full correlation but its first separated window is 0.765 below 0.8; it is rejected, and no threshold was relaxed. Historical report funkwhale-canonical-2026-10-23T06-07-34-865Z.json is preserved.

identityMetadata.mp3Id3: Bounded ID3v2.4 frame inspection for the Chris/Kai files finds no TSRC, recording MusicBrainz UFID/TXXX identifier or usable ISRC.
identityMetadata.oggComments: A bounded first-256-KiB ASCII-key scan of the NIN OGG finds no ISRC= or MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID=. It is not an exhaustive parser for every possible container/tag encoding.
identityMetadata.musicbrainzBridge: Technically plausible when a real source recording MBID exists: query the public recording's ISRCs and compare to the canonical ISRC. That identity path is not established for these three sources, whose identifiers are missing; do not replace acoustic verification by title matching.
identityMetadata.musicbrainzReadProbe: One anonymous Pages-origin lookup of /ws/2/isrc/GBKPL1370800?fmt=json returns readable CORS HTTP404 Not Found; this proves only a readable request and missing indexed identifier, not a valid MBID-to-ISRC bridge control.
identityMetadata.recordingVersusMaster: MusicBrainz documentation defines a recording before final mastering; recording MBID alone does not identify one exact final master.

delivery.chrisAndKai: Observed complete files are served directly by open.audio without a signed query or declared validity period. No permanent-availability guarantee is inferred.
delivery.nin: The listen endpoint redirects to the pod's Wasabi storage using a signed URL with declared 3600-second validity; only host/expiry flags are recorded, never the signed URL. Re-resolve the stable listen locator when needed.
delivery.codec: The tested NIN upload is OGG, while Chris/Kai are MP3. Desktop Chrome playback does not establish iPhone codec/background compatibility.

funkwhale.targetCorpus: Node-only bounded public queries for Epoitaitaye and Pirritx returned valid empty results on this one pod. No claim that the song is absent everywhere, no Epoitaitaye recovery claimed.

navidrome.finding: Owners may create public track/album/artist/playlist shares that listeners can use without accounts, but this is not a global anonymous library-search API. Subsonic access still authenticates users. A voluntarily published public share could be a future input if its owner makes catalog metadata and CORS access available; no such broad canonical source was verified here.

audiomack.finding: Official documentation still uses OAuth 1.0a; its non-user-authenticated read example requires both the application's consumer key and consumer secret. No new safe secretless static playback path was found. No borrowed web/mobile application credentials were used.

bandcamp.finding: The previous public-search challenge and authenticated purchased-collection Subsonic review remain the evidence; this round does not claim that every public Bandcamp stream is impossible or reclassify those prior probes as fresh successes.

nextTechnicalStep: A separate design/implementation gate is warranted for a generic public-Funkwhale adapter with canonical identity verification, version/anonymous-setting checks, bounded processing and stable locators. The current three sources lack identifiers, so a fast metadata-only identity adapter is not yet justified. A mobile-safe excerpt verifier or a separately verified identity cache is still needed; no production code is enabled by this QA report.
remainingLimits: Only approximately 30-second official excerpts are acoustically compared, not the unreferenced remainder of every master.

No real corpus of covers/remixes/medleys has calibrated this waveform verifier; the existing distinct-song negative and withheld-window rejection are useful but insufficient by themselves for arbitrary catalogs.
The diagnostic uses desktop page decoding/FFT work, not a mobile memory-budgeted worker pipeline or globally enforced runtime deadline.
Physical Android/iPhone screen-off, background analysis, next-track preparation and codec behavior remain unverified for this new provider.
Do not infer offline download permission from anonymous playback or from a metadata license field alone.
The new positive coverage does not establish universal commercial-catalog availability.
